title: Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness

paper.title: Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: In Empresses in the Palace ( 甄bsmi嬛gbsn传), a consort congratulates a newly pregnant rival with a single warm line, 「到底是富察姐姐有福气，三五日间就有喜了。」(“Sister Fucha is truly blessed, with child in just a handful of days.”). The words are impeccably kind, yet everyone in the hall knows the Emperor has scarcely visited her, so the congratulation quietly asks how the child could be his. The Empress catches the barb and cannot smile; a less astute consort takes it as sincere praise. This is mock politeness, a pragmatic register in which politeness is the weapon rather than the message ( Culpeper, 1996 ; Haugh, 2015 ) . Reading it requires recovering the speaker’s true intent, noticing that emotion and linguistic surface point in opposite directions, and tracking which listeners decode the attack and which take it at face value ( Bell, 1984 ) . Figure 1 shows how a single expert-anchored annotation captures all three layers, and how the same structure later becomes training signal. We study whether LLMs understand mock politeness, whether this ability can be trained into a small model, and how the training signal contributes to its performance. Existing resources provide limited scale and annotation detail for these questions. The largest prior Chinese mock-politeness evaluation contains 100 items with three-way labels and no theory-of-mind dimension ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , and the classic Chinese implicature benchmark is nearly saturated by strong models ( Yue et al., 2024 ) . Our answer to the first question is ZhenhuanBench, a 1,592-item benchmark whose gold labels derive from 47 hours of expert commentary aligned to the original screenplay. Each aligned utterance carries the speaker’s real intent, an emotion–language mismatch label, and per-listener uptake judgments, and from one annotation we derive four tasks probing intent, second-order theory of mind, multi-listener uptake, and Culpeper-style politeness classification. Text-only evaluation spans 34 LLMs. GPT-6 Astra leads the leaderboard with 73.48 overall and 58.37 on listener reactions; Gemini 3.7 Flash leads the MCQ tasks with 78.97 (§ 4 ). Providing expert commentary raises Gemma-4-31B’s hidden-set accuracy from 65.7 to 85.2. Figure 1: Overview of ZhenhuanBench and CPR-GRPO. (1) 47 hours of expert commentary become 1,506 structured annotations and four tasks, with 81.4 percent of candidate items rejected by quality gates. (2) A sample scene with multi-listener context translated into derived tasks T1–T4. (3) Training that reuses annotations as rewards and traces through Compress, Probe, and Replenish iterations (§ 5.4 ). Our training study asks how to use these expert interpretations to train mock-politeness understanding. Annotation-Grounded Verifiable Rewards (AGVR) turn the annotated relations into supervision for an 8B model. With 338 traces and LoRA, an 8B model rises from 36.8 to 55.7 on the leaderboard’s MCQ tasks under supervision plus one GRPO round, above GPT-5, and gold traces beat chain-of-thought distilled from Kimi-K2.6 on identical items. Diagnosing why further RL saturates, we find the gap between pass@ k k and greedy decoding shrinks 7.5 × \times after correction for multiple-choice chance; the set of recoverable items decreases with each GRPO round. This diagnosis yields CPR-GRPO, a Compress–Probe–Replenish loop that directs further supervision from existing gold traces toward recoverable errors. The 8B model reaches 67.0 on the leaderboard's MCQ tasks, and 74.5 under the training-matched hidden protocol. The trained model also improves over Base on Chinese and English sarcasm tests and retains its aggregate accuracy under character renaming. In summary, our contributions are as follows: • We construct ZhenhuanBench (§ 3 ), the largest theory-grounded Chinese mock-politeness benchmark, whose expert-anchored annotations each yield four tasks over one scene, carry graded multi-source provenance, and double as training signal. • We develop CPR-GRPO (§ 5.1 , § 5.4 ) to train mock-politeness understanding from limited expert annotations, combining judge-free AGVR rewards with chance-corrected selection and weighting of existing gold traces. With 338 traces, the 8B model reaches 67.0 on the leaderboard’s MCQ tasks. • We present extensive experiments and findings (§ 4 , § 5 ). Text-only evaluation covers 34 LLMs, including controlled reasoning comparisons. Training controls show that gold annotation outperforms teacher distillation and interface-only SFT enables subsequent GRPO gains; chance correction reduces the estimated recoverable gap by 7.5 × \times .

sections.heading: Chinese pragmatics benchmarks.
sections.text: SwordsmanImp evaluates sitcom implicature and is nearly saturated ( Yue et al., 2024 ) , the Mask of Civility targets mock politeness directly but is small, coarse-grained, and unreleased ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , and broader suites such as PUB lack the multi-listener dimension ( Sravanthi et al., 2024 ) . LLM pragmatic competence is uneven and tuning-sensitive ( Hu et al., 2023 ; Ruis et al., 2023 ) , and computational politeness predicts perceived politeness from surface features ( Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil et al., 2013 ) rather than asking whether a polite surface hides hostile intent. ZhenhuanBench is an order of magnitude larger than the closest mock-politeness resource, adds per-listener uptake and mismatch structure, and is designed to be trainable (Table A.1 , Appendix A ).

sections.heading: Theory of mind and social intelligence.
sections.text: Machine ToM is usually probed with synthetic false-belief vignettes ( Le et al., 2019 ; Kim et al., 2023 ; Gandhi et al., 2023 ) , on which strong models remain brittle ( Sap et al., 2022 ) , while broader benchmarks test social commonsense or interactive episodes ( Sap et al., 2019 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) and multimodal work reads deception, first impressions, and multi-speaker structure from what is visible and audible ( Kang et al., 2025 ; Kang et al., 2026b ; Ouyang et al., 2025 ) . Related systems span interactive digital humans ( Cai et al., 2025 ) , social video generation ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) , narrative agents ( Huang et al., 2025 ) , and proactive assistance with temporal memory ( Gong et al., 2026a ; Gong et al., 2026b ) . ZhenhuanBench instead isolates the case where the signal is the language itself, with second-order questions from natural dialogue rather than constructed vignettes, several co-present listeners, and expert-documented rather than stipulated gold.

sections.heading: Distillation and RLVR.
sections.text: Rationale-based training uses human explanations ( Camburu et al., 2018 ) and model-generated reasoning ( Hsieh et al., 2023 ; Zelikman et al., 2022 ) ; our traces are instead programmatic rewrites of human-anchored annotation (§ 5.2 ). RLHF trains models from human preferences ( Ouyang et al., 2022 ) , while RLVR methods such as GRPO use verifiable outcomes, chiefly in mathematics and code ( Shao et al., 2024 ; DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025 ) , with recent work on social coordination ( Kang et al., 2026a ) ; AGVR uses exact matches against annotation fields to score pragmatic judgments. Yue et al. (2025) show that RLVR sharpens rather than expands ability, which we replicate and refine with chance correction. Our GRPO adopts DAPO’s zero-variance filtering and asymmetric clip ( Yu et al., 2025 ) . Where variance curricula reweight by raw variance ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) , off-policy guidance mixes gold into rollout groups ( Yan et al., 2025 ) , and self-distillation retrains on model outputs ( Gulcehre et al., 2023 ) , our loop assigns additional gold supervision to examples in a chance-corrected recoverable band. Chance correction is a classical psychometric tool ( Cohen, 1960 ) ; to our knowledge, no prior work has used it to gate RL training.

sections.heading: 3.1 Expert Commentary to Structured Gold
sections.text: We construct gold labels by extracting and auditing interpretations from expert commentary, with corroborating evidence retrieved from an independent English recap podcast and the source novel. Our primary source is the first 110 parts (47 hours of audio) of an ongoing video commentary series on Empresses in the Palace by a dedicated analyst ( Shulan Xiaojiejie, 2025 ) , whose close readings of individual lines provide exactly the intent-level analysis the task needs (source selection and reception in Appendix A ). We transcribe the commentary with Whisper ( Radford et al., 2023 ) , align commentary passages to the 18,297-utterance screenplay (1,214 scenes), and extract 1,506 alignments, each pairing an utterance with the expert’s reading. Cross-source corroboration uses two additional textual sources. Chasing Dramas , an independent English recap podcast ( Karen and Cathy, 2019 ) , contributes 68 episode transcripts (about 249k words), and the source novel by Liu Lianzi ( Liu Lianzi, 2007 ) contributes 1.26M characters including inner monologue. We index both sources with BGE-M3 ( Chen et al., 2024 ) and retrieve passages for each alignment to compare the commentary’s interpretation with the podcast’s account and the novel’s narration. An LLM extractor converts each alignment into four structured fields with verbatim quote anchoring, and a separate audit pass checks fidelity to the commentary (Appendix A ). real_intent states what the speaker is actually doing; emotion_language_mismatch labels affect against surface as aligned , partial_mismatch , or inverted , operationalizing implicational mismatch ( Haugh, 2015 ) ; third_party_reactions lists each listener present with an uptake judgment ( yes , no , partial ) and a one-sentence reason, operationalizing audience design ( Bell, 1984 ) ; and rhetoric_sub_type supports Culpeper-style classification ( Culpeper, 1996 ) .

sections.heading: 3.2 Tasks
sections.text: From each alignment we derive up to four items. T1 asks the speaker’s true intent (4-way MCQ), the implicature-recovery problem of Grice (1975) . T2 asks what a named listener privately concludes (4-way MCQ), a second-order theory-of-mind judgment ( Premack and Woodruff, 1978 ; Perner and Wimmer, 1985 ) . T3 asks for free-text descriptions of every listener’s reaction (scored by an LLM judge at evaluation only), operationalizing audience design ( Bell, 1984 ) . T4 asks for a three-way politeness classification, genuine politeness , mock politeness , or overt impoliteness , the face-based contrast of politeness theory ( Brown and Levinson, 1987 ) operationalized through Culpeper (1996) . Deriving multiple tasks from one annotation enables cross-task consistency and per-alignment diagnostics unavailable to independent-item benchmarks (§ 4.4 ). Item construction enforces an anti-leakage checklist, with neutral phrasing, scene truncation before consequences unfold, length-balanced options, and three option permutations per MCQ (Appendix A ). sections.heading: 3.3 Splits and Scale
sections.text: ZhenhuanBench contains 1,592 items, split into 791 public, 319 hidden-test, and 482 training items with episode-level isolation between training and hidden episodes (Figure 2 ; per-task-by-split counts in Appendix A ). Sampling ran in two symmetric passes over the full commentary to avoid coverage bias. T4 is the scarcest task (212 items) because it requires a confident Culpeper class from the commentary, while T3 contributes 429 free-text items that no MCQ-only protocol would cover. Training and hidden sets share no episode. All splits use the same drama and cast. Figure 2: ZhenhuanBench composition (1,592 items). Inner ring, the three splits (training and hidden episode-disjoint); outer ring, tasks T1–T4 shaded dark to light. Full counts in Appendix A .

sections.heading: 3.4 Quality
sections.text: During construction, every MCQ passes an options-only guessing filter using Claude Haiku-4.5 or GPT-4o-mini: the probe attempts the item from the answer options alone, with the scene withheld, and any item it can solve without the scene is rewritten, removing answer-selection artifacts in the spirit of adversarial dataset filtering ( Le Bras et al., 2020 ; Gururangan et al., 2018 ) . Across two assembly passes the item writer proposed 8,544 candidates and the automated checks rejected 81.4 percent, leaving the 1,592 final items (full funnel in Table A.3 ). Each item records its primary source, supporting quotations, and any cross-source corroboration. The gold label is anchored in the expert commentary for all 1,592 items, verbatim in 823 of them and as a supported paraphrase in the remaining 769, and 1,047 items (65.8 percent) additionally carry a quoted secondary passage that corroborates the same reading, 1,023 citing the English podcast and 28 the novel, with 4 items citing both. A gt_strength field grades this support from 1 to 3 (79, 1,303, and 210 items), so the benchmark can be filtered by how independently each label is attested. On the public set, mean discrimination—the score difference between the upper and lower halves of a 24-model analysis subset ranked by overall score—is positive for all four tasks, from + 0.16 +0.16 to + 0.24 +0.24 .

sections.heading: 4.1 Protocol
sections.text: Prompts provide the scene, cast, target utterance, and question ( P_context ). MCQs use JSON answers, exact-match scoring, and majority voting over three option permutations. Qwen3.8-Max scores T3 reactions against the gold descriptions on a 0/1/2 scale, with temperature 0 and thinking disabled (Appendix D ). Each T3 item averages its listener scores and divides by two; the overall score averages all 791 items. Controlled reasoning comparisons fix the model version and vary its reasoning setting (Appendix G.1 ).

sections.heading: 4.2 Leaderboard
sections.text: GPT-6 Astra leads Table 1 with 73.48 overall, followed by Gemini 3.7 Flash (72.28). Kimi K3 is the highest-scoring open-weight model at 66.76. DeepSeek V4 Pro scores highest on speaker intent (T1), while GPT-6 Astra leads on listener judgments (T2/T3). GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 3.7 Flash tie on politeness classification (T4), and Gemini also leads the MCQ tasks with 78.97. Predicting each listener’s reaction in free text remains difficult, with the best T3 score reaching only 58.37. Using Qwen3.8-Max and Claude Sonnet-4.6 as alternative T3 judges yields highly similar model rankings across 34 configurations, with Spearman correlations of 0.985 0.985 for T3 and 0.999 0.999 for overall scores. Appendix F.1 reports detailed cross-judge results. Training gains. CPR raises Qwen3-8B’s MCQ accuracy from 36.75 to 67.01 and its overall score from 34.20 to 56.69. Its T3 score is close to Base (27.39 versus 26.94). The training analysis in § 5 examines how annotation traces and RL contribute to the MCQ gains. Reasoning budgets. Increasing reasoning effort does not consistently improve mock-politeness understanding. DeepSeek V4 Pro improves from 58.36 overall with thinking off to 68.44 at max effort. Qwen3.8-Max performs best with thinking off (63.43), while Qwen3.8-27B peaks at low effort (54.64). The benefits of additional reasoning are model-dependent rather than uniformly positive (Appendix G.1 ). Character-name sensitivity. On 508 quality-checked items, two consistent renamings change CPR’s mean accuracy from 63.39 to 64.07, versus 36.22 to 32.48 for Base and 67.91 to 58.17 for Qwen3.8-Max. The intervention changes names and aliases while preserving dialogue and role relations (Appendix G.4 ). CPR retains its accuracy under character renaming, whereas Base and Qwen3.8-Max are more sensitive to character-name cues.

sections.heading: 4.3 Text Ablations and Oracle Commentary
sections.text: On the hidden set we vary the prompt for three models (base 8B, our trained model, Gemma-4-31B). Knowledge-enhanced prompting, which injects the textbook definition of mock politeness and helped in prior work ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , hurts all three models here, by − 11.5 -11.5 , − 15.8 -15.8 , and − 4.6 -4.6 points respectively (Table B.1 ), with verbatim prompts in Appendix B . Removing the cast block barely matters. Adding full scene context raises accuracy by 3.7 points for Gemma and 6.5 points for CPR, while lowering Base accuracy by 3.3 points. Appending a short excerpt of the expert’s commentary (an oracle hint) lifts Gemma-4-31B to 85.2, the base model to 60.6, and our model to 75.5. The commentary supplies the expert’s interpretation of the target utterance, including its implied intent and listeners’ understanding. Subtitle-cropped frames yield no significant gain over mismatched frames; audio helps MiniCPM-o-2.6 ( + 3.1 +3.1 ) and leaves Gemini-2.5-Pro unchanged (Appendix E ). Model Consist. sections.heading: 4.4 Schema-Enabled Diagnostics
sections.text: Because multiple tasks share an alignment, we can measure whether a model understands a scene coherently. Cross-task consistency (all sibling MCQs correct) separates models far more sharply than accuracy (Table 2 ). For Kimi-K2.6 versus Base 8B, MCQ accuracy differs by 1.8 × \times (66.8/36.8), compared with 3.5 × \times for consistency (42.9/12.2); GPT-5 and Haiku-4.5 score 27.6 and 19.9. Coherent scene-level understanding is rarer than per-item accuracy suggests. The trained model raises consistency from 12.2 to 37.2 (above Sonnet-4.6) and reduces the none-right rate from 41.0 to 10.9, the lowest value in Table 2 . Mismatch-confusion analysis appears in Appendix F.1 .

sections.heading: 5 Training Study
sections.text: Understanding mock politeness requires relating polite wording to speaker intent and listener uptake in context. Our annotations record these relations as intent, emotion–language mismatch, and listener reactions, providing supervision for training. As RL gains saturate, CPR-GRPO uses a chance-corrected recovery estimate to select and weight existing gold traces for further supervision. Unless noted otherwise, training uses Qwen3-8B with LoRA ( Hu et al., 2022 ) ; Appendix F.4 replicates the supervised stage, one GRPO round, and one full loop iteration on further backbones. Unless noted, we evaluate on the MCQ items of the held-out hidden test, which shares no episode with training, using paired bootstrap tests. The public-set results use the MCQ protocol of Table 1 , reported as the micro average over its MCQ tasks (T1, T2, T4); the overall column of Table 1 additionally includes judge-scored T3.

sections.heading: 5.1 AGVR: Annotation-Grounded Verifiable Rewards
sections.text: For SFT, AGVR converts each aligned annotation into a five-step trace: evidence, mismatch, per-listener uptake, intent, and a JSON answer. Each step is instantiated programmatically from gold fields. For RL, the same fields define string-verifiable rewards (answer, mismatch, and uptake matches plus a − 0.5 -0.5 format gate). Training rewards are computed directly from the gold annotation fields. Supervision lifts the 8B model from 36.8 to 52.3 on this metric and one GRPO round on the same annotations to 55.7, above GPT-5 (53.3); and on the 253 items the teacher Kimi-K2.6 could itself solve, gold traces beat its rejection-sampled chain-of-thought 55.6 to 49.5. Auxiliary reward heads reduce variability across seeds (Appendix F.2 ). SFT accuracy increases with gold-trace count (Figure F.1 , Appendix F.2 ). Figure 3: Leaderboard-protocol MCQ accuracy (public set). Training raises 8B accuracy from 36.8 to 67.0; the shaded band spans GPT-5 to Kimi-K2.6.

sections.heading: 5.2 Effects of Output Format and Supervised Content
sections.text: GRPO from the base model changes accuracy by − 0.5 -0.5 points ( p = 0.9 p{=}0.9 ). A two-by-two study (Table F.2 , Appendix F.2 ) separates the interface (the five-step-plus-JSON output format that the reward function parses and scores) from the content (gold reasoning). Interface-only SFT replaces reasoning spans with placeholders and reaches 56.9/55.6; subsequent GRPO adds + 3.3 +3.3 / + 3.2 +3.2 . Gold reasoning supplied as unparseable prose scores 1.9/3.7, with 95 percent parse failures and 51 percent zero-variance rollout groups. Interface-only SFT thus enables GRPO gains in both tested seeds. A shuffled-content control gains + 2.8 +2.8 , compared with + 25.5 +25.5 for the full recipe. Answer-plus-intent supervision without the five-step structure scores 59.3 versus 62.0 (Table 3 ). sections.heading: 5.3 Chance-Corrected Analysis of GRPO
sections.text: Figure 4: Pure GRPO plateaus near 70 on the hidden set (shaded band); adding Replenish (orange, two seeds) reaches 74.5 at round 4. GRPO after SFT adds + 4 +4 to + 5 +5 points to greedy accuracy. pass@8 stays flat (93.1 to 93.5) while greedy and majority vote rise, replicating the sharpening view of RLVR ( Yue et al., 2025 ) . The pass@16-minus-greedy gap is 31.4 points; random guessing already gives pass@16 above 99 percent on 4-way items. Chance-corrected, the recoverable excess is only 4.2 points (RL) and 4.8 (SFT), a 7.5 × \times inflation that declines monotonically down the pipeline (5.7, 4.8, 4.2) even as greedy accuracy climbs thirty points. The recoverable band decreases during training. Grouping greedy-wrong items by chance-corrected recovery shows that fewer items remain recoverable as GRPO gains diminish; the round-3 increment is + 0.9 +0.9 .

sections.heading: 5.5 Training Controls
sections.text: Table F.3 (Appendix F.3 ) reports the training controls. Anchoring the same gold traces inside RL groups as off-policy members, in the spirit of LUFFY ( Yan et al., 2025 ) , yields 65.3, compared with 66.7 for GRPO. Pure GRPO scores 69.4 at round 5. sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.text: ZhenhuanBench evaluates mock politeness through speaker intent, emotion–language mismatch, and listener uptake. GPT-6 Astra leads the leaderboard with 73.48 overall, while listener-reaction prediction remains difficult across models. Gold annotation traces outperform teacher reasoning on matched items, and interface-only supervision enables subsequent GRPO gains. Chance correction reduces the estimated recoverable performance gap by 7.5 × \times ; CPR-GRPO uses this estimate to weight gold supervision and raises an 8B model’s public MCQ accuracy from 36.8 to 67.0. Fixed-checkpoint evaluation shows gains on Chinese and English sarcasm tasks, and character renaming preserves CPR’s aggregate accuracy. Larger reasoning budgets improve DeepSeek’s performance; Qwen models peak at off or low effort. Together, these findings show how expert pragmatic interpretations can support both the evaluation and training of models to understand mock politeness.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.text: The benchmark draws its scenes from a single Chinese drama. Training and hidden splits use different episodes but share characters and setting. Overlap with model pretraining data is unknown. T3 is scored by an LLM judge. Its absolute scores vary across judges.

sections.heading: Ethics Statement
sections.text: ZhenhuanBench draws on publicly accessible, copyrighted creative works: a television screenplay, fan commentary, a recap podcast, and a novel, cited in § 3.1 . The release contains structured annotations, short evidence quotations, and episode and scene references; it excludes the original video and audio. The commentary author’s account is cited, and the reception statistics in Appendix A come from public profile pages. The dialogue and characters are fictional. Items contain indirect verbal aggression characteristic of mock politeness, with no slurs or graphic material. Potential misuse includes assistance with manipulative writing. Our experiments train and evaluate comprehension.

sections.heading: Annotation schema.
sections.text: Each of the 1,506 alignments pairs one screenplay utterance with the expert’s reading of it and carries four structured fields. real_intent is a one-sentence statement of what the speaker is doing (e.g., 借道贺暗指皇上极少召幸, 公开质疑龙种真伪, “using a congratulation to hint that the Emperor rarely summons her, publicly casting doubt on whether the child is genuine,” for the running example of Figure 1 ). emotion_language_mismatch takes one of aligned , partial_mismatch , or inverted , operationalizing the implicational mismatch account of mock politeness. third_party_reactions lists every listener present with an uptake tag in { yes , no , partial } and a one-sentence reason. rhetoric_sub_type records the rhetorical device and supports the Culpeper three-way classification.

sections.heading: Extraction and audit.
sections.text: Extraction runs in two passes. The first pass converts a commentary span into candidate fields with a verbatim quote anchor from the commentary, and a second audit pass verifies each field against its anchor and repairs or discards unsupported fields. On the full set the audit flagged 292 of the 1,506 alignments (19.4 percent), the leading error types being plot summary written as intent (136), character misattribution (62), hallucinated detail (61), and event misattribution (33), and repaired 269 of them against their anchors.

sections.heading: Item assembly.
sections.text: Items are assembled under an anti-leakage checklist. Questions use neutral phrasing that does not presuppose hostility, scenes are truncated before the consequences of the utterance unfold, options are length-balanced within 15 percent, every MCQ is evaluated under three option permutations, and sibling items derived from one alignment never share option text. sections.heading: Primary-source selection.
sections.text: We selected the commentary for its line-by-line analysis of dialogue and quotable evidence for the annotated interpretations. The account is certified by Bilibili as a well-known film-and-television creator and has about 491,000 followers; the 47-video archive of parts 1–110 used in our corpus has 32.8 million plays (accessed 2026-07-31). Each extracted field carries a verbatim quote anchor and undergoes an audit against the commentary. The English recap podcast and source novel provide cross-source corroboration (§ 3.4 ).

The knowledge-enhanced condition P_definition prepends the following definition, given verbatim with an English gloss. 【Haugh 2014 mock politeness 定义 (理论参考)】mock politeness 指外形上礼貌 (敬语/谦辞/客套) 但内核为非礼貌 (攻击/讽刺/施压) 的语言现象。形式与功能错位, 用礼貌形式包装非礼貌意图。识别要点 (1) 表面话语寄存器为礼貌 (2) 真实意图为攻击或操控 (3) 听者通常听得懂, 但因规范无法当场揭破。 English gloss. [Haugh 2014 mock politeness definition, theoretical reference] Mock politeness is speech whose form is polite (honorifics, deference, courtesy formulas) but whose substance is impolite (attack, sarcasm, coercion). Form and function are misaligned, a polite wrapper around an impolite intent. Cues are (1) a polite surface register, (2) a real intent to attack or manipulate, (3) listeners who usually understand but cannot expose the attack on the spot. The oracle condition appends a block labeled 【专家解说提示】(“expert commentary hint”) containing the expert’s commentary excerpt for the aligned utterance. The scaffold prompt used for training and hidden-set evaluation appends a five-step output contract requiring <evidence> , <mismatch> , <listeners> , and <intent> tags before the JSON answer. These prompt comparisons disable thinking. Reasoning-setting experiments use the configurations in Appendix G.1 . RL-trained checkpoints repeated prompt text when evaluated with a thinking template absent from training.

sections.heading: Appendix D T3 Judge
sections.text: T3 responses are scored per listener using the following rubric. The leaderboard and reasoning comparisons use Qwen3.8-Max, temperature 0, thinking disabled, and a 256-token output cap. The judge receives the scene, speaker, target utterance, listener, reference reaction, and predicted reaction. Model identities and previous scores are omitted. 【任务】对比 模型输出的 listener 反应描述 vs gold listener 反应描述, 评分 0/1/2。【评分细则】0 分: 模型反应与 gold 主旨明显不同/完全没答到点/方向相反。1 分: 部分正确, 抓到了 gold 的某一面但缺关键细节或有小错。2 分: 与 gold 主旨一致, 关键判断 (听懂/没懂/反击/顺从) 都对, 用词可以不同。 English gloss. [Task] Compare the model’s description of each listener’s reaction against the gold description and score 0/1/2. [Rubric] 0, the response clearly departs from the gold reading, misses the point entirely, or points the opposite way. 1, partially correct, capturing one aspect of the gold but missing key details or making a minor error. 2, consistent with the gold reading, with the key judgments (understood or not, strikes back or complies) all correct; wording may differ. Scores are averaged over listeners and normalized to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] per item. The judge appears only at evaluation time and never in training.

sections.heading: An audio probe.
sections.text: We test whether prosodic cues improve performance using the same protocol on the 138-item set. Each item pairs its MCQ with the 8-second original-audio clip of the utterance moment (16 kHz mono, cut by the same Whisper timestamps), and three conditions are compared, T (text only), TA (text plus the item’s own audio), and AC (text plus another item’s audio under the same fixed derangement). We compare matched and mismatched audio against the text-only baseline to distinguish their effects. On both MiniCPM-o-2.6 and Gemini-2.5-Pro ( Comanici et al., 2025 ) , matched audio beats the mismatched control by an identical TA − - AC of + 3.6 +3.6 , significantly so in both cases, yet the decomposition against text-only is opposite. For MiniCPM, matched audio raises accuracy over text (TA − - T = + 3.1 =+3.1 [ + 0.2 , + 6.3 ] [+0.2,+6.3] ) while a random clip is neutral (AC − - T = − 0.5 =-0.5 ). For Gemini, matched audio leaves accuracy unchanged (TA − - T = + 0.0 =+0.0 [ − 3.1 , + 3.1 ] [-3.1,+3.1] ) and mismatched audio lowers accuracy (AC − - T = − 3.6 =-3.6 [ − 6.8 , − 0.5 ] [-6.8,-0.5] ). Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B ( Xu et al., 2025 ) , has negative point estimates for both audio comparisons (TA − - T = − 2.9 =-2.9 , TA − - AC = − 2.4 =-2.4 , both intervals spanning zero), and its visual comparison gives (TV − - VC = − 0.2 =-0.2 ). Matched-minus-mismatched differences reflect changes in either condition; comparison with text alone distinguishes improvements from losses under mismatched inputs. The same confound explains the vision numbers, where both matched and mismatched frames raise Gemini’s accuracy over text (TV − - T = + 4.3 =+4.3 , VC − - T = + 6.8 =+6.8 ) so TV − - VC is negative. Audio improves MiniCPM in this evaluation; corresponding gains are absent for Gemini and Qwen3-Omni.

sections.heading: F.4 Cross-Backbone Replication
sections.text: We apply the same recipe to GLM-4-9B ( Team GLM et al., 2024 ) and Qwen3-14B. On GLM-4-9B, AGVR SFT lifts the hidden-set score from 42.1 to 54.2 (paired + 12.0 +12.0 , 95% CI [ + 4.2 , + 19.9 ] [+4.2,+19.9] , p = 0.004 p=0.004 ). sections.heading: G.2 External Evaluation of Fixed Checkpoints
sections.text: We evaluate the Qwen3-8B Base, SFT, GRPO, and CPR checkpoints without training on target-dataset labels. SFT is trained on 338 gold traces. MultiPragEval ( Park et al., 2024 ) contributes 300 Chinese and 300 English pragmatic-inference questions; accuracy averages three option permutations. ToSarcasm ( Liang et al., 2022 ) uses its 973-item Chinese test set, evaluated both with the topic and after removing it, and reports binary Macro-F1. English iSarcasmEval ( Abu Farha et al., 2022 ) uses 1,400 Task-A items (sarcastic-class F1) and 200 Task-C pairs (accuracy under the original order). Each pair contrasts a sarcastic text with its non-sarcastic rephrase. Table 4 in § 5.6 reports the results. CPR improves over Base on all six evaluations, including + 4.94 +4.94 Macro-F1 on ToSarcasm and + 3.33 +3.33 sarcastic-class F1 on iSarcasmEval A. Removing the topic raises ToSarcasm scores for every checkpoint.

FGVIrony training examples sharing a news component with the test set are removed; development data are grouped by news component. CPED uses dialogue-disjoint warm-start and subsequent training pools, in balanced and natural-frequency regimes. Balanced sampling takes 24 warm-start and 48 pool examples per class; natural sampling keeps the same total sizes. Both regimes use the same full official test set. SemEval uses the official cleaned test inputs joined to gold labels by identifier. sections.heading: Training.
sections.text: All runs use LoRA rank 64 and scaling 128, two warm-start SFT epochs, and learning rates 10 − 5 10^{-5} for SFT and 5 × 10 − 6 5\times 10^{-6} for GRPO. Compress uses six sampled responses per item; Probe uses 16, with chance level 1 / K 1/K , excess threshold 0.06, and replenishment weights 4/2/1. Rewards check the gold class; malformed answers receive − 0.5 -0.5 . FGVIrony runs three cycles and selects checkpoints on development Macro-F1. CPED and SemEval use one fixed cycle. Checkpoint selection is completed before test evaluation. Wrong-only replenishment samples greedy errors after Compress and matches CPR’s supervised output-token budget. Evaluation uses greedy decoding with thinking disabled. Table 5 in § 5.6 reports the three-seed means. CPR exceeds GRPO by 2.33, 3.03, 7.50, and 4.10 points across the four settings, and also exceeds wrong-only replenishment. Prioritizing recoverable errors is more effective here than sampling all greedy errors indiscriminately.

sections.heading: Construction and checks.
sections.text: We exclude 20 pilot scenes from the 585 public MCQs, leaving 525 candidates. Two consistent pseudonym maps replace names, aliases, and name-bearing titles throughout the inputs while retaining rank, relationships, dialogue, and option meanings. Programmatic checks verify reversible replacement. Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 review semantic consistency without access to gold answers. Seventeen unresolved or name-dependent items are excluded, yielding 508 items from 170 scenes. The final set is frozen before evaluation.

Learn more × Back to arXiv License: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license arXiv:2610.26059v1 [cs.CL] 19 Oct 2026 Honeyed Words, Hidden Daggers: Benchmarking and Training LLMs to See Through Mock Politeness 1 Introduction In Empresses in the Palace ( 甄bsmi嬛gbsn传), a consort congratulates a newly pregnant rival with a single warm line, 「到底是富察姐姐有福气，三五日间就有喜了。」(“Sister Fucha is truly blessed, with child in just a handful of days.”). The words are impeccably kind, yet everyone in the hall knows the Emperor has scarcely visited her, so the congratulation quietly asks how the child could be his. The Empress catches the barb and cannot smile; a less astute consort takes it as sincere praise. This is mock politeness, a pragmatic register in which politeness is the weapon rather than the message ( Culpeper, 1996 ; Haugh, 2015 ) . Reading it requires recovering the speaker’s true intent, noticing that emotion and linguistic surface point in opposite directions, and tracking which listeners decode the attack and which take it at face value ( Bell, 1984 ) . Figure 1 shows how a single expert-anchored annotation captures all three layers, and how the same structure later becomes training signal. We study whether LLMs understand mock politeness, whether this ability can be trained into a small model, and how the training signal contributes to its performance. Existing resources provide limited scale and annotation detail for these questions. The largest prior Chinese mock-politeness evaluation contains 100 items with three-way labels and no theory-of-mind dimension ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , and the classic Chinese implicature benchmark is nearly saturated by strong models ( Yue et al., 2024 ) . Our answer to the first question is ZhenhuanBench, a 1,592-item benchmark whose gold labels derive from 47 hours of expert commentary aligned to the original screenplay. Each aligned utterance carries the speaker’s real intent, an emotion–language mismatch label, and per-listener uptake judgments, and from one annotation we derive four tasks probing intent, second-order theory of mind, multi-listener uptake, and Culpeper-style politeness classification. Text-only evaluation spans 34 LLMs. GPT-6 Astra leads the leaderboard with 73.48 overall and 58.37 on listener reactions; Gemini 3.7 Flash leads the MCQ tasks with 78.97 (§ 4 ). Providing expert commentary raises Gemma-4-31B’s hidden-set accuracy from 65.7 to 85.2. Figure 1: Overview of ZhenhuanBench and CPR-GRPO. (1) 47 hours of expert commentary become 1,506 structured annotations and four tasks, with 81.4 percent of candidate items rejected by quality gates. (2) A sample scene with multi-listener context translated into derived tasks T1–T4. (3) Training that reuses annotations as rewards and traces through Compress, Probe, and Replenish iterations (§ 5.4 ). Our training study asks how to use these expert interpretations to train mock-politeness understanding. Annotation-Grounded Verifiable Rewards (AGVR) turn the annotated relations into supervision for an 8B model. With 338 traces and LoRA, an 8B model rises from 36.8 to 55.7 on the leaderboard’s MCQ tasks under supervision plus one GRPO round, above GPT-5, and gold traces beat chain-of-thought distilled from Kimi-K2.6 on identical items. Diagnosing why further RL saturates, we find the gap between pass@ k k and greedy decoding shrinks 7.5 × \times after correction for multiple-choice chance; the set of recoverable items decreases with each GRPO round. This diagnosis yields CPR-GRPO, a Compress–Probe–Replenish loop that directs further supervision from existing gold traces toward recoverable errors. The 8B model reaches 67.0 on the leaderboard's MCQ tasks, and 74.5 under the training-matched hidden protocol. The trained model also improves over Base on Chinese and English sarcasm tests and retains its aggregate accuracy under character renaming. In summary, our contributions are as follows: • We construct ZhenhuanBench (§ 3 ), the largest theory-grounded Chinese mock-politeness benchmark, whose expert-anchored annotations each yield four tasks over one scene, carry graded multi-source provenance, and double as training signal. • We develop CPR-GRPO (§ 5.1 , § 5.4 ) to train mock-politeness understanding from limited expert annotations, combining judge-free AGVR rewards with chance-corrected selection and weighting of existing gold traces. With 338 traces, the 8B model reaches 67.0 on the leaderboard’s MCQ tasks. • We present extensive experiments and findings (§ 4 , § 5 ). Text-only evaluation covers 34 LLMs, including controlled reasoning comparisons. Training controls show that gold annotation outperforms teacher distillation and interface-only SFT enables subsequent GRPO gains; chance correction reduces the estimated recoverable gap by 7.5 × \times . 2 Related Work Chinese pragmatics benchmarks. SwordsmanImp evaluates sitcom implicature and is nearly saturated ( Yue et al., 2024 ) , the Mask of Civility targets mock politeness directly but is small, coarse-grained, and unreleased ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , and broader suites such as PUB lack the multi-listener dimension ( Sravanthi et al., 2024 ) . LLM pragmatic competence is uneven and tuning-sensitive ( Hu et al., 2023 ; Ruis et al., 2023 ) , and computational politeness predicts perceived politeness from surface features ( Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil et al., 2013 ) rather than asking whether a polite surface hides hostile intent. ZhenhuanBench is an order of magnitude larger than the closest mock-politeness resource, adds per-listener uptake and mismatch structure, and is designed to be trainable (Table A.1 , Appendix A ). Theory of mind and social intelligence. Machine ToM is usually probed with synthetic false-belief vignettes ( Le et al., 2019 ; Kim et al., 2023 ; Gandhi et al., 2023 ) , on which strong models remain brittle ( Sap et al., 2022 ) , while broader benchmarks test social commonsense or interactive episodes ( Sap et al., 2019 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) and multimodal work reads deception, first impressions, and multi-speaker structure from what is visible and audible ( Kang et al., 2025 ; Kang et al., 2026b ; Ouyang et al., 2025 ) . Related systems span interactive digital humans ( Cai et al., 2025 ) , social video generation ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) , narrative agents ( Huang et al., 2025 ) , and proactive assistance with temporal memory ( Gong et al., 2026a ; Gong et al., 2026b ) . ZhenhuanBench instead isolates the case where the signal is the language itself, with second-order questions from natural dialogue rather than constructed vignettes, several co-present listeners, and expert-documented rather than stipulated gold. Distillation and RLVR. Rationale-based training uses human explanations ( Camburu et al., 2018 ) and model-generated reasoning ( Hsieh et al., 2023 ; Zelikman et al., 2022 ) ; our traces are instead programmatic rewrites of human-anchored annotation (§ 5.2 ). RLHF trains models from human preferences ( Ouyang et al., 2022 ) , while RLVR methods such as GRPO use verifiable outcomes, chiefly in mathematics and code ( Shao et al., 2024 ; DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025 ) , with recent work on social coordination ( Kang et al., 2026a ) ; AGVR uses exact matches against annotation fields to score pragmatic judgments. Yue et al. (2025) show that RLVR sharpens rather than expands ability, which we replicate and refine with chance correction. Our GRPO adopts DAPO’s zero-variance filtering and asymmetric clip ( Yu et al., 2025 ) . Where variance curricula reweight by raw variance ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) , off-policy guidance mixes gold into rollout groups ( Yan et al., 2025 ) , and self-distillation retrains on model outputs ( Gulcehre et al., 2023 ) , our loop assigns additional gold supervision to examples in a chance-corrected recoverable band. Chance correction is a classical psychometric tool ( Cohen, 1960 ) ; to our knowledge, no prior work has used it to gate RL training. 3 ZhenhuanBench 3.1 Expert Commentary to Structured Gold We construct gold labels by extracting and auditing interpretations from expert commentary, with corroborating evidence retrieved from an independent English recap podcast and the source novel. Our primary source is the first 110 parts (47 hours of audio) of an ongoing video commentary series on Empresses in the Palace by a dedicated analyst ( Shulan Xiaojiejie, 2025 ) , whose close readings of individual lines provide exactly the intent-level analysis the task needs (source selection and reception in Appendix A ). We transcribe the commentary with Whisper ( Radford et al., 2023 ) , align commentary passages to the 18,297-utterance screenplay (1,214 scenes), and extract 1,506 alignments, each pairing an utterance with the expert’s reading. Cross-source corroboration uses two additional textual sources. Chasing Dramas , an independent English recap podcast ( Karen and Cathy, 2019 ) , contributes 68 episode transcripts (about 249k words), and the source novel by Liu Lianzi ( Liu Lianzi, 2007 ) contributes 1.26M characters including inner monologue. We index both sources with BGE-M3 ( Chen et al., 2024 ) and retrieve passages for each alignment to compare the commentary’s interpretation with the podcast’s account and the novel’s narration. An LLM extractor converts each alignment into four structured fields with verbatim quote anchoring, and a separate audit pass checks fidelity to the commentary (Appendix A ). real_intent states what the speaker is actually doing; emotion_language_mismatch labels affect against surface as aligned , partial_mismatch , or inverted , operationalizing implicational mismatch ( Haugh, 2015 ) ; third_party_reactions lists each listener present with an uptake judgment ( yes , no , partial ) and a one-sentence reason, operationalizing audience design ( Bell, 1984 ) ; and rhetoric_sub_type supports Culpeper-style classification ( Culpeper, 1996 ) . 3.2 Tasks From each alignment we derive up to four items. T1 asks the speaker’s true intent (4-way MCQ), the implicature-recovery problem of Grice (1975) . T2 asks what a named listener privately concludes (4-way MCQ), a second-order theory-of-mind judgment ( Premack and Woodruff, 1978 ; Perner and Wimmer, 1985 ) . T3 asks for free-text descriptions of every listener’s reaction (scored by an LLM judge at evaluation only), operationalizing audience design ( Bell, 1984 ) . T4 asks for a three-way politeness classification, genuine politeness , mock politeness , or overt impoliteness , the face-based contrast of politeness theory ( Brown and Levinson, 1987 ) operationalized through Culpeper (1996) . Deriving multiple tasks from one annotation enables cross-task consistency and per-alignment diagnostics unavailable to independent-item benchmarks (§ 4.4 ). Item construction enforces an anti-leakage checklist, with neutral phrasing, scene truncation before consequences unfold, length-balanced options, and three option permutations per MCQ (Appendix A ). Best scores across all models are bold. 3.3 Splits and Scale ZhenhuanBench contains 1,592 items, split into 791 public, 319 hidden-test, and 482 training items with episode-level isolation between training and hidden episodes (Figure 2 ; per-task-by-split counts in Appendix A ). Sampling ran in two symmetric passes over the full commentary to avoid coverage bias. T4 is the scarcest task (212 items) because it requires a confident Culpeper class from the commentary, while T3 contributes 429 free-text items that no MCQ-only protocol would cover. Training and hidden sets share no episode. All splits use the same drama and cast. Figure 2: ZhenhuanBench composition (1,592 items). Inner ring, the three splits (training and hidden episode-disjoint); outer ring, tasks T1–T4 shaded dark to light. Full counts in Appendix A . 3.4 Quality During construction, every MCQ passes an options-only guessing filter using Claude Haiku-4.5 or GPT-4o-mini: the probe attempts the item from the answer options alone, with the scene withheld, and any item it can solve without the scene is rewritten, removing answer-selection artifacts in the spirit of adversarial dataset filtering ( Le Bras et al., 2020 ; Gururangan et al., 2018 ) . Across two assembly passes the item writer proposed 8,544 candidates and the automated checks rejected 81.4 percent, leaving the 1,592 final items (full funnel in Table A.3 ). Each item records its primary source, supporting quotations, and any cross-source corroboration. The gold label is anchored in the expert commentary for all 1,592 items, verbatim in 823 of them and as a supported paraphrase in the remaining 769, and 1,047 items (65.8 percent) additionally carry a quoted secondary passage that corroborates the same reading, 1,023 citing the English podcast and 28 the novel, with 4 items citing both. A gt_strength field grades this support from 1 to 3 (79, 1,303, and 210 items), so the benchmark can be filtered by how independently each label is attested. On the public set, mean discrimination—the score difference between the upper and lower halves of a 24-model analysis subset ranked by overall score—is positive for all four tasks, from + 0.16 +0.16 to + 0.24 +0.24 . 4 Evaluating Frontier Models 4.1 Protocol Prompts provide the scene, cast, target utterance, and question ( P_context ). MCQs use JSON answers, exact-match scoring, and majority voting over three option permutations. Qwen3.8-Max scores T3 reactions against the gold descriptions on a 0/1/2 scale, with temperature 0 and thinking disabled (Appendix D ). Each T3 item averages its listener scores and divides by two; the overall score averages all 791 items. Controlled reasoning comparisons fix the model version and vary its reasoning setting (Appendix G.1 ). 4.2 Leaderboard GPT-6 Astra leads Table 1 with 73.48 overall, followed by Gemini 3.7 Flash (72.28). Kimi K3 is the highest-scoring open-weight model at 66.76. DeepSeek V4 Pro scores highest on speaker intent (T1), while GPT-6 Astra leads on listener judgments (T2/T3). GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 3.7 Flash tie on politeness classification (T4), and Gemini also leads the MCQ tasks with 78.97. Predicting each listener’s reaction in free text remains difficult, with the best T3 score reaching only 58.37. Using Qwen3.8-Max and Claude Sonnet-4.6 as alternative T3 judges yields highly similar model rankings across 34 configurations, with Spearman correlations of 0.985 0.985 for T3 and 0.999 0.999 for overall scores. Appendix F.1 reports detailed cross-judge results. Training gains. CPR raises Qwen3-8B’s MCQ accuracy from 36.75 to 67.01 and its overall score from 34.20 to 56.69. Its T3 score is close to Base (27.39 versus 26.94). The training analysis in § 5 examines how annotation traces and RL contribute to the MCQ gains. Reasoning budgets. Increasing reasoning effort does not consistently improve mock-politeness understanding. DeepSeek V4 Pro improves from 58.36 overall with thinking off to 68.44 at max effort. Qwen3.8-Max performs best with thinking off (63.43), while Qwen3.8-27B peaks at low effort (54.64). The benefits of additional reasoning are model-dependent rather than uniformly positive (Appendix G.1 ). Character-name sensitivity. On 508 quality-checked items, two consistent renamings change CPR’s mean accuracy from 63.39 to 64.07, versus 36.22 to 32.48 for Base and 67.91 to 58.17 for Qwen3.8-Max. The intervention changes names and aliases while preserving dialogue and role relations (Appendix G.4 ). CPR retains its accuracy under character renaming, whereas Base and Qwen3.8-Max are more sensitive to character-name cues. 4.3 Text Ablations and Oracle Commentary On the hidden set we vary the prompt for three models (base 8B, our trained model, Gemma-4-31B). Knowledge-enhanced prompting, which injects the textbook definition of mock politeness and helped in prior work ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , hurts all three models here, by − 11.5 -11.5 , − 15.8 -15.8 , and − 4.6 -4.6 points respectively (Table B.1 ), with verbatim prompts in Appendix B . Removing the cast block barely matters. Adding full scene context raises accuracy by 3.7 points for Gemma and 6.5 points for CPR, while lowering Base accuracy by 3.3 points. Appending a short excerpt of the expert’s commentary (an oracle hint) lifts Gemma-4-31B to 85.2, the base model to 60.6, and our model to 75.5. The commentary supplies the expert’s interpretation of the target utterance, including its implied intent and listeners’ understanding. Cross-task consistency (all sibling MCQs correct) separates models far more sharply than accuracy (Table 2 ). For Kimi-K2.6 versus Base 8B, MCQ accuracy differs by 1.8 × \times (66.8/36.8), compared with 3.5 × \times for consistency (42.9/12.2); GPT-5 and Haiku-4.5 score 27.6 and 19.9. Coherent scene-level understanding is rarer than per-item accuracy suggests. The trained model raises consistency from 12.2 to 37.2 (above Sonnet-4.6) and reduces the none-right rate from 41.0 to 10.9, the lowest value in Table 2 . Mismatch-confusion analysis appears in Appendix F.1 . 5 Training Study Understanding mock politeness requires relating polite wording to speaker intent and listener uptake in context. Our annotations record these relations as intent, emotion–language mismatch, and listener reactions, providing supervision for training. As RL gains saturate, CPR-GRPO uses a chance-corrected recovery estimate to select and weight existing gold traces for further supervision. Unless noted otherwise, training uses Qwen3-8B with LoRA ( Hu et al., 2022 ) ; Appendix F.4 replicates the supervised stage, one GRPO round, and one full loop iteration on further backbones. Unless noted, we evaluate on the MCQ items of the held-out hidden test, which shares no episode with training, using paired bootstrap tests. The public-set results use the MCQ protocol of Table 1 , reported as the micro average over its MCQ tasks (T1, T2, T4); the overall column of Table 1 additionally includes judge-scored T3. 5.1 AGVR: Annotation-Grounded Verifiable Rewards For SFT, AGVR converts each aligned annotation into a five-step trace: evidence, mismatch, per-listener uptake, intent, and a JSON answer. Each step is instantiated programmatically from gold fields. For RL, the same fields define string-verifiable rewards (answer, mismatch, and uptake matches plus a − 0.5 -0.5 format gate). Training rewards are computed directly from the gold annotation fields. Supervision lifts the 8B model from 36.8 to 52.3 on this metric and one GRPO round on the same annotations to 55.7, above GPT-5 (53.3); and on the 253 items the teacher Kimi-K2.6 could itself solve, gold traces beat its rejection-sampled chain-of-thought 55.6 to 49.5. Auxiliary reward heads reduce variability across seeds (Appendix F.2 ). SFT accuracy increases with gold-trace count (Figure F.1 , Appendix F.2 ). GPT-6 Astra leads the leaderboard with 73.48 overall, while listener-reaction prediction remains difficult across models. Gold annotation traces outperform teacher reasoning on matched items, and interface-only supervision enables subsequent GRPO gains. Chance correction reduces the estimated recoverable performance gap by 7.5 × \times ; CPR-GRPO uses this estimate to weight gold supervision and raises an 8B model’s public MCQ accuracy from 36.8 to 67.0. Fixed-checkpoint evaluation shows gains on Chinese and English sarcasm tasks, and character renaming preserves CPR’s aggregate accuracy. Larger reasoning budgets improve DeepSeek’s performance; Qwen models peak at off or low effort. Together, these findings show how expert pragmatic interpretations can support both the evaluation and training of models to understand mock politeness. Limitations The benchmark draws its scenes from a single Chinese drama. Training and hidden splits use different episodes but share characters and setting. Overlap with model pretraining data is unknown. T3 is scored by an LLM judge. Its absolute scores vary across judges. Ethics Statement ZhenhuanBench draws on publicly accessible, copyrighted creative works: a television screenplay, fan commentary, a recap podcast, and a novel, cited in § 3.1 . The release contains structured annotations, short evidence quotations, and episode and scene references; it excludes the original video and audio. The commentary author’s account is cited, and the reception statistics in Appendix A come from public profile pages. The dialogue and characters are fictional. Items contain indirect verbal aggression characteristic of mock politeness, with no slurs or graphic material. Potential misuse includes assistance with manipulative writing.
